topic: Data storage and opt-out tracking setup
summary_markdown:
The conversation covered several data infrastructure points. First, the need to manage data volume was discussed; specifically, adjusting the retention policy for `raw seen` data from a month's worth to a much shorter period or moving most of it to hot storage was proposed to prevent cold storage capacity issues.

Second, a plan was established to track MAC addresses for users who opt-out (unsubscribe). It was decided that a new table, potentially named `device_optout`, should be created in PostgreSQL. The mechanism for populating this table will involve creating an endpoint that pulls data from WordPress and is best handled by 'Zhenya' (Жека), with the goal of integrating these jobs into the main data API.

Finally, a temporary pause on the `raw seen` insertion was implemented at the request of [me] and subsequently reactivated.
decisions: The retention policy for raw seen data needs adjustment to reduce cold storage load.
A new PostgreSQL table (`device_optout`) will be created to store MAC addresses of unsubscribed users.
An endpoint connecting WordPress to populate the opt-out table will be built by 'Zhenya'.
Raw seen insertion was temporarily paused and later reactivated.
action_items: Adjust raw seen data retention policy/storage location.
Build WordPress integration endpoint for opt-out tracking (assigned to Zhenya).
